extracted.intended_audience: prospective News21 applicants, journalism students, journalism educators, media partners and general public
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive overview of the Carnegie-Knight News21 national student investigative reporting initiative run by Arizona State University's Walter Cronkite School, including program structure, participant responsibilities, partners and republishing policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project output standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Students report and produce in-depth, multimedia projects for major media outlets, such as The Washington Post, NBC News and USA Today.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects are expected to be in-depth and multimedia in nature and are produced for distribution through major media organizations; examples of previous investigations include topics such as hate groups, drinking water, police reform, health disparities, juvenile justice and gun rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program components / participant timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Students selected for the News21 program study a topic in-depth during a virtual spring seminar, followed by a 10-week reporting fellowship during the summer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sequence is a preparatory virtual seminar in spring, then an intensive 10-week summer newsroom fellowship where students report and produce their projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work setting and reporting expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Students work out of a newsroom at the Cronkite School and travel the country — and sometimes to other countries — to report and produce their projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are expected to operate from the program newsroom and undertake travel as necessary to pursue reporting for their investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant profile / selection target
rubrics_metrics.description: The program 'brings top journalism students from across the country' to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection targets high-performing journalism students from different universities; individual fellows receive support from their universities and various foundations, news organizations and philanthropic partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and funding expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: The John S. and James L. Knight Foundation provides core support for the News21 program; individual fellows are supported by their universities and a variety of foundations, news organizations and philanthropic partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and participants should expect a program funded by foundations and partner organizations; this explains resource availability and institutional backing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Republishing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Republish our work. It's all Creative Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News21 content is released under a Creative Commons license and may be republished according to that license's terms.
